questions.question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.

options.text: I was rently at a literary festival.
I was recently at a litrary festival.
I was recently at a literary festival.
I was recently at a literery fstival.

questions.solution:

questions.question:

questions.solution:

• **When we rearrange** the parts according to option** SRPQ,** we get a coherent and logical sentence:
 
• **"S.** The residents of Noida can now get their pets like dogs or cats
 
• **R. **registered with the local authority through a mobile phone
 
• **P. **application, which can also be used to log complaints about

• The phrase** 'according to officials' **at the end refers to the** source of this information.**
 
• **This makes a **logical, clear, and grammatically correct sentence.

Therefore, the **correct order** of sentence is: **'SRPQ'.**

questions.question:
Select the option that will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement'.

Dad said that, "__She would have been a great sister if she was just a bit more careful__".

options.text: that, "She would have been a great sister if she were just a bit more careful"
"She would have been a great sister if she were just a bit more careful"
"She would have been a greatest sister if she was just a bit more careful"

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• This is because, in English grammar, **when referring to hypothetical situations or conditions** that are contrary to fact, **we often use "were"** **instead** of** "was" **after "if" even when the subject is singular.
 
• This is a usage pattern known as the subjunctive mood.
 
• So,* "if she were just a bit more careful"* is **more grammatically correct than** *"if she was just a bit more careful".*
 
• Also, we use** 'that'** to **introduce reported speech** when the words are not the speaker’s exact words (i.e., when the speaker is paraphrasing, summarizing, or interpreting the original speaker’s words). So,** 'Dad said that' **is *appropriate here.*

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is:* "Dad said that, 'She would have been a great sister if she were just a bit more careful'".*

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

Nandini said, "I bought a pen yesterday."

options.text: Nandini said she did bought a pen the previous day.
Nandini said that she had bought a pen the previous day.
Nandini said that she had bought a pen yesterday.
Nandini says that she had bought a pen the previous day.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **sentence is in direct speech** and it needs to be changed to indirect speech.
 
• When** converting direct to indirect speech, **present tense verbs are often changed to past tense, and words referring to near time ('yesterday' in this case) need to be changed to refer to a more distant time ('the previous day').
 
• The verb** "bought"** is in the past simple, so it **changes to past perfect ("had bought")** in reported speech.
 
• The phrase *"I bought a pen yesterday"* thus **changes to** *"she had bought a pen the previous day".*

Therefore, the **correct indirect form** of the given sentence is *"Nandini said that she had bought a pen the previous day."*
